item.title: Play the New World vs. World Borderlands Map Beta on November 10
item.dc:creator: The Guild Wars 2 Team
item.description:
Learn how we'll be developing this map alongside the WvW community!

Read More
item.content:encoded:
Greetings Gamers!

Back in June, we announced that the Guild Wars 2® team was developing the first new borderlands map for World vs. World in over a decade and we’re building it alongside the players who live and breathe it. Our first beta test for the new map begins on November 10, so mark your calendars! Today, we’d like to share an update on our progress so far, what we’re aiming to achieve, and give you an early look at some gray-box screenshots of the map.

Lessons from the Desert

When we developed the Desert Borderlands, we didn’t show the map to the community until it was in a mostly final state. This didn’t afford the team with ample flexibility to respond to feedback, especially when it came to changing the layout of the map. This time, just like we did with the Push PvP game mode, we’re involving you much earlier in the process. When you get your hands on the map during the first beta, it will be in a gray-box state, meaning that the art and assets won’t be final, making it much easier for us to make changes. We’ll be able to alter the layout of the map and objective placement, which will impact things like travel time and combat flow. The competitive team’s top priority is making sure this new map captures what players love about the current World vs. World battlegrounds while building an experience that is fresh and exciting.

For the first beta, we won’t be introducing any new map mechanics like we did with the Desert Borderlands. We found that we threw a lot at the community all at once, such as controlling the elemental shrines for special bonuses and the energy cannon event in the oasis. While we’re interested in exploring these sorts of additions, we want to save that for when we’re further along. Instead, we’d like to focus the first beta on gathering feedback on the map and objective layout. We want to focus on how it feels to navigate the map, where battles occur, and how long it takes to get from place to place. After we’re satisfied with the layout, we’ll move on to things like unique map mechanics.

Battle in Ascalon

When this beta begins, to maximize the play time on the new map, all borderlands maps will be replaced with the new gray-box map. Eventually, we plan to have this new map permanently replace the current Green Alpine Borderlands, making each borderlands unique with a distinct theme. Set during the cataclysmic events of the Searing in Ascalon, our new map will allow our World vs. World players to explore a battlefield of one of the most iconic areas in Tyria. The Ascalon-themed map will encapsulate areas from pre-Searing and post-Searing with tie-ins to both humans and the war-driven charr of that age.

Get Ready for the Beta on November 10

After the first beta test, we will be running more beta tests before this map is released to the live game. Subsequent beta tests will have changes to the map and objectives based on the feedback we gather from this first one, and potentially some brand-new map and objective mechanics. We’re hoping to take advantage of the betas to see what could work not only for this new map, but also as possible additions to WvW as a whole.

When we get closer, we’ll be opening up a feedback thread on the official forums to gather your thoughts. We’re looking forward to shaping the new borderlands map with the World vs. World community. When the time comes, make sure to be vocal about what you like and don’t like!

Until next time, as always, we’ll see you in the Mists!

item.title: Play the Finale of Visions of Eternity Today with “Code of Creation”
item.dc:creator: The Guild Wars 2 Team
item.description:
Explore the depths of Castora, face high-stakes raid and fractal encounters, and experience the epic conclusion to Guild Wars 2's latest expansion!

Read More
item.content:encoded:
Guild Wars 2®: Visions of Eternity™ wraps up its dramatic story arc today with the release of “Code of Creation.” Today’s update is brimming with new content and rewards to pursue, so strap in as we give you the full rundown. To kick things off, watch the “Code of Creation” trailer below and check out the full release notes for all the specifics.

What’s New?

In addition to the new map, story chapters, and endgame encounters we previewed last week, “Code of Creation” is packed with new content. Here’s a complete breakdown of everything arriving in today’s release:

  • New map: Leyspring Hollows
  • Six climactic story chapters
  • Fractal: Solitary Throne
  • Raid encounter: Nexus of Eternity
  • Convergence: Nexus of Eternity
  • Legendary Sword: Wages of Stars
  • Mastery line: Rift Amplification
  • Wizard’s Vault seasonal refresh
  • Scads of new rewards and achievements

Become a Master of Rift Amplification

With the final quarterly release of Guild Wars 2: Visions of Eternity, players will be able to unlock a new mastery line called Rift Amplification that grants a fresh approach to how they can engage with rifts across Tyria. Throughout the story in Castora, players might have noticed something different about the rifts here, namely that they had Inquest! Our allies in the Tyrian Alliance have been investigating how the Inquest has been able to harness these powers, and in “Code of Creation,” they’ve finally found the answer.

With Rift Amplification, players will be granted access to four new mastery tiers:

  • Rift Tears: This mastery grants you the ability to use the Heart of the Obscure to find alternate routes to the active rift you’re tracking. Now, instead of following the magics to their source, you’ll be able to go to Rift Tears that exist in nonactive rift areas spread across Castora. When interacted with, they will teleport you directly to the active rift, getting you to the fun, faster!
  • Overcharged Rifts: After the first part of a rift event is complete, you’ll now be given the option to “overcharge” the rift before the boss appears. By overcharging the rift with a motivation of the same tier, you’ll be faced with a greater challenge from the summoned boss and an additional threat from the instability of the rift itself. Those who overcome this additional challenge will receive additional rewards.
  • Tearing Across Tyria: As your bond with the Heart of the Obscure deepens, you’ll now be able to utilize Rift Tears across any rifts in Tyria.
  • Overcharge Tyria: Finally, as a master of rifts, you will now be able to overcharge all rifts in Tyria that can be opened with the Heart of the Obscure.

New Treasures Await!

“Code of Creation” wouldn’t be complete without some awesome new rewards to seek and claim for your own. Playing through the story will reward players with the Tenebral Ward armor set, perfect for channeling a dark, gothic knight vibe. On the opposite end of the spectrum, you can craft arms from the Shining Ward weapon set. These ornate implements feature intricate designs and are made from a stunning mixture of ivory, teal, and royal blue materials.

The new legendary sword, Wages of Stars, is as magnificent as the cosmos. This brilliant blade sparkles with a galaxy of stars and is unique in that it follows its wielder by hovering nearby when sheathed. This sword is truly a treasure to behold, with its starry footfalls, a draw animation that produces constellations, and a dazzling finisher effect!

New rewards from the Nexus of Eternity Convergence and raid encounter include two new combat tonics for those who can’t get enough of Vloxx! Volatile Ascension is a new infusion that also drops from the Convergence, but we’ll let you discover what its visual effects are for yourself.

And of course, there are many other rewards to collect, including unique one-off weapons, miniatures, seer-themed homestead decorations, emotes, relics, and more!

A New Season of Wizard’s Vault Rewards

The Wizard’s Vault stock has been refreshed with new rewards! Spend your astral acclaim on the Gwyl Knight weapon set, or complete your Ward Hunter armor set with the new mask, leggings, coat, and cape. Tyrian birders won’t want to miss the Bird Pond Chair, where you can relax with a few of your avian friends.

As we pause our expansions to make room for the Hall of Monuments and quality-of-life updates, rest assured that we’ll continue to rotate the Wizard’s Vault rewards on a similar cadence as we’ve done previously. And don’t forget that all our past cosmetic rewards are always available in the Wizard’s Vault Legacy tab, so you never have to fear missing out!

Watch Streams to Earn Twitch Drops

From now until September 20, you can earn exciting Twitch Drops just by watching your favorite Guild Wars 2 streamers. Watch a total of six hours before 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time (UTC-7) on September 20 to unlock all available rewards, including the brand-new Arcane Occultist’s Hat!

Here are the goodies you can earn:

  • One Hour: Item Booster
  • Two Hours: Mini Piglet
  • Four Hours: How to Dance, Volume 1
  • Six Hours: Arcane Occultist’s Hat

Visions of Eternity Vinyl Soundtrack

Immerse yourself in the rich soundscape of Guild Wars 2‘s sixth expansion with the official soundtrack of Guild Wars 2: Visions of Eternity. Composed by Bryan Atkinson, Ben Ash, Brendon Williams, and Catherine Nguyen, this soundtrack features 37 evocative tracks.

Preorder the deluxe 2xLP 180-gram Blood Orange vinyl today for $39.99!

Looking Ahead

“Code of Creation” is out now, but the fun doesn’t stop there. From our brand-new Dismount Rush event later this month to the return of Fractal Incursion, along with the beta for our new WvW map, Extra Life, and our first Hall of Monuments update, there’s a lot to look forward to before the end of the year.

Check out the full event schedule below, or read last week’s blog for a deeper breakdown of what’s coming next.

The entire Guild Wars 2 team poured their hearts into Guild Wars 2: Visions of Eternity and we can’t wait to see your reactions to “Code of Creation.” Tell us what you think on our official forums and Discord server.

Be safe, have fun, and game on!

item.title: “Code of Creation” Concludes Visions of Eternity on September 15
item.dc:creator: The Guild Wars 2 Team
item.description:
The finale to Guild Wars 2's latest expansion is packed with a new map, raid encounter, fractal, story chapters, and more!

Read More
item.content:encoded:
Greetings, Tyrians!

The final chapter of Guild Wars 2®: Visions of Eternity™ drops September 15. Next week, “Code of Creation” will send players into the depths of Castora as they seek to stop Vloxx from achieving his goals throughout six climactic new story chapters. All eyes are on you, Commander, and here is what you need to know about next week’s update.

Guild Wars 2: Visions of Eternity—”Code of Creation”

When the commander and their allies departed from the port of Lion’s Arch, everyone suspected typical Inquest antics—cold and calculating leadership, merciless creations, and a propensity for cruelty in pursuit of innovation. All things the commander certainly faced during their adventure on Castora, but Vloxx proved to be a more complex opponent. His mission was a ruse, viewing the Inquest simply as tools while he sought to remedy something far more severe. Now, the former Inquest director has taken up the mantle of eternity while Kuda has taken up the Inquest he left behind.

In the final update of Guild Wars 2: Visions of Eternity, the commander and Isgarren must coordinate with their allies to fight back against those who threaten everything they’ve built and fought to preserve.

Leyspring Hollows

At the start of “Code of Creation,” you’ll venture deep into the cavernous expanse of Leyspring Hollows in pursuit of both Kuda’s Inquest and Vloxx.

The depths are a mysterious place, and like many things you’ve encountered on Castora, they’re as dangerous as they’re disarmingly beautiful. As you traverse the twisting veins of the leyspring in pursuit of your enemies, you’ll uncover the seer doyen’s greatest secret and the heart of his people’s spiritual undertaking on Castora. The Stewards of Galdra, “living” remnants of this once great society, are eager to keep these secrets from the clutches of your enemies and have offered their aid in your quest.

Although Vloxx abandoned the Inquest, they now pose a threat that cannot be ignored. Kuda is unhinged; she’s been waiting her entire life for this moment—and no one is taking it away from her. Left to their own devices, many of the Inquest are plundering the depths for power. No longer on their heels, you and your allies must make a final stand against them before Kuda pushes the Inquest into a new level of brutality.

Our enemies cannot succeed.

The Depths of Cruelty

In “Code of Creation,” you’ll fight against the Inquest in a multistage meta-event as tensions come to a head with the newly crowned Director Kuda. In the Depths of Cruelty meta, you’ll face a greater challenge than those set before within the expansion. Communication and collaboration will be key in thwarting Kuda’s plans, with the weight of your decisions having a direct impact on swinging the tide of battle in your favor.

Unlike the other meta-events in Guild Wars 2: Visions of Eternity, the Depths of Cruelty is set on a three-hour cycle rather than two, which is similar to Convergences. We’ve also shuffled the Shackles of the Ancients meta-event start time five minutes earlier. We decided on these changes to allow for each meta-event within Guild Wars 2: Visions of Eternity, as well as the Convergence, to run with a reduced chance of potential competition with the other’s start times. That way, you’ll be able to go from event to event, across each map, with minimal disruption.

Another reason for the adjustment is to allow you more time to engage with content on the map before the meta-event begins. Similar to maps like Dragon’s End and Amnytas, Leyspring Hollows will close after the meta-event is completed, but instead of closing immediately, you’ll get a prompt to move to a new map within one hour.

Changing Up Convergences

For this release, you’ll participate in a new Convergence where you’ll find yourself coming head-to-head against in the Nexus of Eternity. You’ll face challenges that call back to experiences and mechanics throughout other parts of Tyria.

Unlike the Mount Balrior and Outer Nayos Convergences, where you clash against a rotation of bosses, the Nexus of Eternity Convergence contains one robust encounter with multiple distinct phases. With this change, you’ll be able to experience the full variety of mechanics with each run and the choices you make will keep the encounter feeling fresh.

We’ve also adjusted the risk vs. reward elements of essence gathering. You must now push yourself to the limit by gathering max stacks of the essence before they can be cleared. Though, doing so will now reward a powerful ability based on your profession, allowing you to turn the tides of battle in your favor.

Prepare Your Squad for New Challenges

In addition to a new Convergence, the Nexus of Eternity has also been adapted to test your mettle as a challenging raid encounter. This encounter requires a squad of ten players to work together to face the great challenges that await them in the finale of Guild Wars 2: Visions of Eternity.

A new fractal, Solitary Throne, is also releasing with “Code of Creation.” Groups of up to five players can explore what happens when a single being harnesses too much power. Avoid hazards while navigating a mysterious, celestial environment to reach and defeat the Eternal Tyrant himself.

If you’re hungry for a more severe challenge, we will also be releasing Challenge Modes for the Convergence, raid encounter, and fractal two weeks after “Code of Creation” launches on September 29. Following that, the Legendary Mode for the raid encounter will launch on October 13.

Coming Up This Fall

“Code of Creation” kicks off a season that is jam-packed with bonus events, festivals, and game updates. The complete roadmap is detailed below, but let’s discuss some of the highlights.

Later this month, we’ll be debuting a new event called “Dismount Rush” that will offer temporary bonus rewards for forgoing your mounts in content designed before mounts were introduced. This fall, the Fractal Incursion event will return with new rewards, and we’ll be kicking off the beta for our new WvW map where your feedback will help shape its development. Then, we have our annual Extra Life charity game day and accompanying in-game event, which is always a highlight of our year. Finally, we’ll cap off the year with our first Hall of Monuments update, allowing players to start earning rewards for Guild Wars 3™!

Get ready for what we have coming up:

 

September

  • September 29–October 6: Dismount Rush Event
  • September 29: Fractal Challenge Mode: Solitary Throne
  • September 29: Raid Challenge Mode: Nexus of Eternity
  • September 29: Convergence Challenge Mode: Nexus of Eternity

October

  • October 13–November 3: Shadow of the Mad King
  • October 13: Raid Legendary Mode: Nexus of Eternity

November

  • November 10–December 1: Fractal Incursion
  • November 10: Skills and Balance Update
  • November 10: WvW New Map Beta
  • November 10–December 1: Extra Life Bonus Event
  • November 13–14: Extra Life Game Day
  • November 23– December 1: Gnashbash “Birthday” Celebration

December

  • December 8–January 5: Wintersday Festival
  • To Be Announced: Hall of Monuments Begins

Stay tuned for more information in the coming days on our social media channels and our official Discord. We’re looking forward to watching you experience everything we have waiting for you in the “Code of Creation.”

—The Guild Wars 2 Team

item.title: WvW War Score: Beta 2 Results and What’s Next
item.dc:creator: The Guild Wars 2 Team
item.description:
Get the details on what we learned from our recent beta and the changes we're making for Beta 3.

Read More
item.content:encoded:
Hello, Tyrians!

Throughout this year, the Competitive team has been running beta tests to improve how scoring works in World vs. World (WvW). The focus of the betas has been to shift score generation toward tangible player actions like sieging, capturing objectives, and killing players while moving away from passive mechanics like owning objectives over time that can happen whether players are involved or not.

After the first beta, we shared our findings in a retrospective posted on our forums. Today, we’re here to discuss our feedback and changes based on the second War Score beta we ran during the matchup in May. This beta included new placement-based match rewards, a series of scoring adjustments, and the addition of points awarded for upgrading objectives.

Balancing Active and Passive Play

While the first beta started with zero passively gained points aside from supply deliveries, we agreed with players that defending objectives was not adequately rewarding. In response, we adjusted to a good mix of score accrual from holding objectives that still encouraged interaction from enemy teams. Some points were added back to holding tier 3 objectives, but a larger number of points were added to objective tier-ups. This created contention that players could expect and play around instead of having all objectives constantly trickling points.

So how was the balance? After fixing some extreme outliers—dolyak’s deliveries, for instance—we landed on a much healthier spread in Beta 2 compared to Beta 1:

  • Objective captures resulted in roughly 30% of all War Score generated.
  • Player combat was about 25% of all War Score generated.
  • Progress ticks accounted for 5% of the total, but combined with upgrades, holding objectives jumps to 15%.
  • The single largest source of War Score generation was keep captures followed closely by player kills.

For reference, the score breakdown for normal gameplay outside of the betas is roughly 40% player combat and 35% passive objective ticks with objective assaults being only 9% of the total score generation.

Adjustments for Beta 3

Dolyak deliveries are still on the watchlist. Supply is the lifeblood of WvW, so we’re very hesitant to remove scoring from dolyaks entirely even if they do provide a challenge for balancing passive score generation. We will continue to adjust their point value. Additionally, while guard kills do add some flavor with a low barrier to interaction, their total score value outweighs their mechanical contribution to the game mode, so they will no longer reward War Score in Beta 3.

One mechanic in the beta that hasn’t had much attention is scaling score based on player counts. The intent was to encourage player congregation, but the system has been overly complex to balance and not easily understood. Plus, the majority of points being scored were coming from objectives that already had naturally incrementing point values.

Therefore, for Beta 3, we will be removing player count and objective type/tier scaling multipliers for simplicity, though the capability will still be there if we want to bring it back.

Beta 3 will include the return of placement-based match rewards, placement-based skirmish rewards, more balance changes, and boosted points for defensive player kills. For defensive actions, smaller areas around objectives will be used instead of the entire sector.

Another exciting new feature to look forward to is an in-game breakdown of War Score sources. We believe that if there are rewards attached to winning, players deserve more insight into what results in victory and the ability to compare against opponents. We’re looking forward to your feedback on these additions!

What’s Next for WvW?

At the end of the War Score betas, we’re going to have new tech that we can leverage, regardless of whether we permanently adopt the adjusted scoring paradigms or not. This would include keeping the new in-game match scoring breakdown and placement-based rewards locked in to continue incentivizing players to care about scoring.

Lastly, don’t forget we’re also developing a new WvW borderlands map alongside the community. For a refresher on that and our upcoming WvW initiatives, here’s a recap of what our Game Director, Josh Davis, spoke about in June:

Beta 3 will begin in the middle of a matchup, so we want to make you aware in advance.  We’re looking forward to hearing your feedback about our latest changes to War Score when you get to experience it in WvW during Beta 3 running from August 11 until September 4.

We’ll see you in the Mists!

item.content:encoded:
Join us next week for a celebration of our Guild Wars 2® homesteads! Ever since Homesteads were released with Guild Wars 2: Janthir Wilds™, we’ve been in awe of the community’s creative constructions. To celebrate that creativity and encourage new designs, we’re holding the Homestead Design Contest on our official Discord channel starting July 30!

Conjure your best designs in either homestead map and start snapping some screenshots. There’s no specific theme, so let your creativity run wild! Then, submit your screenshots for peer review and a chance to win gem prizes via community vote!

Submissions of 1–10 screenshots will be accepted from July 30 at 9:00 a.m. Pacific Time (UTC-7) until August 6 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time (UTC-7). Community voting will last from the beginning of the entry period on July 30 until August 11 at 2:00 p.m. Pacific Time (UTC-7). At that point, voting will end and winners will be determined by the total number of emoji reactions received. Full rules and eligibility can be found here.

While the contest is running, there will be other reasons to celebrate Homesteads. We’ll have Twitch drops available for watching your favorite Guild Wars 2 streamers starting on July 30. And we’ll be hosting a homestead livestream on Wednesday, August 5 at 12:00 p.m. Pacific Time (UTC-7) on our Twitch channel. Check out Discord next week for more details, but in the meantime, have fun staging your homestead for sharing with the community!

—The Guild Wars 2 Team

item.title: Play Your Way in Guild Wars 2
item.dc:creator: The Guild Wars 2 Team
item.description:
Our partner, Kroof, breaks down the various playstyles of Guild Wars 2.

Read More
item.content:encoded:
With Guild Wars 2® rapidly approaching its 14th anniversary, it’s abundantly clear that there are numerous ways to enjoy the game. For some, the draw is immersing themselves into the lore of Tyria and getting engrossed in the stories of its inhabitants.  For others, it’s tackling the toughest encounters or knocking out every achievement they can.

Whether you spend your time collecting legendary weapons, decking your many characters out in the most fabulous ensembles, or exploring every secret nook in the vast open world, one thing is certain: there’s no wrong way to play Guild Wars 2.

Today, we invite you to go on a journey exploring the various playstyles of Guild Wars 2 with a video from one of our incredible partner program members, Kroof. And over the next few weeks, stay tuned to our social channels and Discord as we invite you to share with us how you play your way.
